examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the MuleSoft Developer I exam?
examDifficulty.summary: The Salesforce Certified MuleSoft Developer exam covers introductory Mule 4 projects, Anypoint Platform and Studio, integrations, DataWeave, event flow, error handling, and batch processing.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 120 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
70% to pass, which is 42 correct answers out of 60.
The official guide expects experience building basic Mule 4 projects with guidance; it does not require a set number of projects or a prior certification.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Use the official exam objectives to plan hands-on practice in Anypoint Studio, DataWeave, integration patterns, error handling, and deployment.

examFormat.heading: MuleSoft Developer I exam format
examFormat.intro: The proctored exam is available online or at a test centre. Prepare for questions across these topics:
bestWayToPass: Practise DataWeave 2.0: Work with map, filter, reduce, and pluck until you can read and write common scripts.
Build Mule flows: Create HTTP-triggered flows with connectors, error handlers, and deployment configuration.
Know the connectors: Review HTTP Listener and Request, database operations, and Salesforce CRUD configuration.
Choose error handlers carefully: Understand On Error Continue, On Error Propagate, and how error types relate.

certificationCard.description: This credential validates foundational Mule 4 development skills, including Anypoint Platform and Studio, integrations, DataWeave transformations, event handling, errors, and batch work. The guide notes that up to five questions may be unscored. The exam is 60 scored questions in 120 minutes, with a 70% pass mark, weighted towards Accessing and Modifying Mule Events and Structuring Mule Applications (10% each).
topics: Deploying and Managing APIs and Integrations (7%)

keyConcepts.h2: MuleSoft Developer I: concepts to review

blocks.heading: Credential and exam information
blocks.body: Salesforce lists the credential as [Salesforce Certified MuleSoft Developer](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/credentials/mulesoftdeveloperi). The [official exam guide](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005298959&language=en_US&type=1) lists 60 multiple-choice questions plus up to five unscored items, a 120-minute limit, 70% passing score, a US$200 registration fee, a US$100 retake fee, and no prerequisite. The guide is aligned to Spring ’24, so verify the current exam outline and [certification pricing](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005298916&language=en_US&type=1) before booking. MuleSoft Developer I is a prerequisite for Developer II.

blocks.heading: Anypoint Platform and the development lifecycle
blocks.body: Anypoint Platform supports the integration lifecycle: design, develop, deploy, and manage. Anypoint Studio is the Eclipse-based environment for building Mule apps. Exchange is a catalog for APIs, connectors, templates, and examples. CloudHub hosts deployed Mule applications as an integration platform service. A common lifecycle is to design an API in API Designer, publish it to Exchange, implement it in Studio, deploy it to CloudHub, and manage it in Runtime Manager.

blocks.heading: Mule events, flows, and messages
blocks.body: A Mule event carries a message through an application. The message contains a payload and attributes; the event can also hold variables and an error when handling a failure. A flow starts with a source such as an HTTP Listener, file listener, or scheduler, then runs processors that transform, route, or call services. A subflow has no source and is called from another flow. Private flows are callable components rather than event sources. Know how the event and message change as processors run.

blocks.heading: DataWeave 2.0 transformations
blocks.body: DataWeave transforms, filters, and maps data. Common functions include map to transform array elements, filter to select elements, reduce to aggregate, pluck to process object entries, and groupBy to organize values by a key. Data types include String, Number, Boolean, Array, Object, Null, and Any. The header declares input and output MIME types. For example, `%dw 2.0 output application/json ---` identifies DataWeave 2 and produces JSON. Practise reading and writing common transformation scripts.

blocks.heading: API-first design with RAML
blocks.body: RAML 1.0 describes REST API contracts. Common parts include baseUri, version, mediaType, data types, traits, and resource types. Exchange API fragments can hold data types, traits, resource types, security schemes, and examples. In API-first work, design and mock the contract, share it for consumer feedback, and then implement it. Exchange’s Mocking Service lets consumers try the contract before implementation is complete.

blocks.heading: Error handling in Mule
blocks.body: Mule error handling uses Try scopes and On Error Continue or On Error Propagate handlers. On Error Continue runs the handler and lets the owning flow finish successfully with the handler’s result. On Error Propagate runs the handler and passes the error to the caller. Error types follow a hierarchy that includes ANY, CONNECTIVITY, EXPRESSION, ROUTING, and SECURITY. Choose a handler based on the error and whether the flow should succeed or return an error.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the MuleSoft Developer I exam
scenarioTips.intro: The exam checks foundational Anypoint skills: building integrations in Studio, using connectors, transforming data with DataWeave, and deploying applications. Practise complete flows and syntax.

blocks.heading: Design Mule 4 flows
blocks.body: Understand flows with event sources, subflows called by reference, and private flows. Track how payload, attributes, and variables change as processors run.

blocks.heading: Work with DataWeave
blocks.body: Practise mapping, filtering, object transformations, reductions, plucking, flattening, and type coercion.

blocks.heading: Configure connectors
blocks.body: Review HTTP Listener and Request, Database, File/FTP, JMS/AMQP, and Salesforce connectors. Learn connection testing, pooling, and reconnection settings.

blocks.heading: Handle errors
blocks.body: Compare Try, On Error Continue, On Error Propagate, and global handlers. Recognize error types such as MULE:CONNECTIVITY and HTTP:UNAUTHORIZED.

blocks.heading: Deploy to CloudHub
blocks.body: Review CloudHub 1.0 environment selection, worker size and count, deployment properties, and application monitoring.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After Developer
nextCertsAfter.intro: Build on your MuleSoft development knowledge with these related Salesforce credentials:

sampleQuestions.question: A flow encounters an error but should still return a successful response to its caller. Which handler should be used?
sampleQuestions.explanation: On Error Continue runs its handler and lets the owning flow finish successfully with the handler result.
whyWrong: Until Successful retries an operation; it does not define the flow’s error response.
A Try scope without a handler does not change the error outcome.
On Error Propagate passes the error to the caller, which receives a failure.

sampleQuestions.question: What information travels in a Mule event?
options: The connector settings from the project
A Mule message with event variables
A payload and a flow reference
sampleQuestions.explanation: The event carries a message with payload and attributes, and it can also contain variables.
whyWrong: The message also includes attributes, and the event can hold variables.
Connectors are configuration, not event data.
Flow references are application components, not event content.

sampleQuestions.question: A DataWeave script receives XML but must write JSON. Where is the output format declared?
options: Only in a Set Payload operation
In the DataWeave header as output application/json
In the input declaration as application/xml
sampleQuestions.explanation: The DataWeave header declares the output MIME type used to serialize the result.
whyWrong: Set Payload does not declare the output MIME type.
Reconnection settings handle connectivity problems.
The input type does not set the output format.

sampleQuestions.question: Which DataWeave function transforms every element in an array?
sampleQuestions.explanation: map applies a transformation to each item and returns an array of the results.
whyWrong: filter selects items but does not transform every item.
reduce combines the items into an accumulated result.
groupBy organizes items under keys.

sampleQuestions.question: In a Mule event, how do attributes differ from variables?
options: They have the same role and lifetime
Attributes persist across all flows while variables do not
sampleQuestions.explanation: Attributes are metadata supplied by a source or operation. Variables are set deliberately and can persist through the flow.
whyWrong: They have different purposes and lifecycles.
Variables can propagate through flow references; the statement reverses their behavior.
Variables are writable values.

sampleQuestions.question: A team wants to agree on the API contract before implementation. Which approach supports this?
options: API-first design with a RAML or OAS specification
Build flows first and document them later
Deploy to production and refine the contract
sampleQuestions.explanation: API-first design defines and reviews the API specification before implementation begins.
whyWrong: A database schema does not define the full API contract.
Documenting after implementation is not API-first.
Production deployment is not a substitute for agreeing on the contract.

sampleQuestions.question: Which component processes large inputs in chunks and tracks errors by record?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Batch Job processes records in blocks and tracks success or failure for individual records.
whyWrong: For Each loops through a collection within a flow without batch job tracking.
Choice routes an event based on conditions.
Scatter-Gather sends an event to multiple routes and combines their results.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Mule router invokes every configured route, waits for each route to finish, and combines the returned results?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Scatter-Gather fans the message out to its routes in parallel, waits for their outcomes, and aggregates the route results.
whyWrong: First Successful tries routes until one succeeds.
Choice selects a route based on a condition.
Round Robin sends events to routes in sequence.

sampleQuestions.question: What is Anypoint Exchange used for?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Exchange is a catalog where teams publish and discover APIs, connectors, templates, and other assets.
whyWrong: Runtime logs are accessed through management and monitoring tools.
Worker metrics are viewed through monitoring tools.
Error handlers are defined in Mule applications.

sampleQuestions.question: Where does an administrator apply runtime API policies such as rate limits or client ID enforcement?
sampleQuestions.explanation: API Manager administers deployed APIs and applies policies through the gateway.
whyWrong: Design Center is used to design APIs.
Studio is the Mule development environment.
MUnit is used to test Mule applications.

sampleQuestions.question: A developer needs automated tests for a Mule flow and wants to mock an outbound connector. Which tool should be used?
sampleQuestions.explanation: MUnit is the Mule application testing framework and supports processor mocking.
whyWrong: Monitoring observes a running application rather than testing its behavior.
Batch jobs process data, not test flows.
A Logger writes diagnostic messages but does not assert behavior.

sampleQuestions.question: Where should a host name that changes between environments be stored?
options: Put it in an externalized property file
Put it in the business payload
Create a flow variable during deployment
sampleQuestions.explanation: Externalized properties let the same application use different values in each environment without code edits.
whyWrong: Hard-coding requires a change for each environment.
Payloads hold business data, not deployment configuration.
Flow variables are event data rather than deployment properties.

sampleQuestions.question: What can a Transform Message component produce?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Transform Message runs DataWeave and writes its result to the payload or a target variable.
whyWrong: API specifications are authored in API design tools or source files.
The build process creates deployment artifacts.
Reconnection policies are connector configuration.

sampleQuestions.question: A downstream service is briefly unavailable and connector calls fail intermittently. Which setting addresses this?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A reconnection strategy retries connectivity failures when a service is temporarily unavailable.
whyWrong: Batching changes record processing, not connection recovery.
Payload size does not affect service availability.
Routing does not resolve connection failures.

sampleQuestions.question: A Try scope uses an On Error Propagate handler. What happens after the handler runs?
options: The error is propagated to the enclosing flow or caller
The error is logged and ignored
The flow continues as if the operation succeeded
sampleQuestions.explanation: On Error Propagate runs the handler and then passes the error upward so the enclosing scope fails.
whyWrong: The error is passed onward rather than only logged.
Handling a flow error does not automatically stop the application.
Continuing successfully is On Error Continue behavior.
